properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 24 at 10:10PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
At 1010 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 18
miles southwest of Cornudas, moving northeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and half inch hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Cornudas.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 24 at 10:01PM MDT until October 26 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, San
Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains and Utah,
including the following areas, Arches/Grand Flat,
Canyonlands/Natural Bridges, La Sal and Abajo Mountains and
Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...Through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, recent burn scars and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm
drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Flooding is imminent or ongoing with additional rounds of showers
and thunderstorms expected through Sunday afternoon. Rivers and
creeks may still experience high waters even after rainfall has
ended.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH NOW IN EFFECT THROUGH SUNDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Mineral, CO; Rio Grande, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 9:56PM MDT until October 25 at 12:15AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding continues along the Rio Grande and downstream
waterways.

* WHERE...Southeastern Mineral County and Rio Grande County...

* WHEN...Until 1215 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will continue along and near the Rio Grande
overnight, especially from near Del Norte to below Monte Vista.
Several roads remain closed and housing areas evacuated due to high
water. While many rivers and streams have already crested, flooding
and high flows will continue tonight, especially around Monte
Vista.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 956 PM MDT, Water levels along the Rio Grande remain high,
especially in the stretch from Del Norte to below Monte Vista,
although the river has crested and levels are forecast to remain
steady or slowly fall overnight.
- Please continue to heed any road closures.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
The Rio Grande from Del Norte to Monte Vista.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 9:54PM MDT until October 25 at 2:00AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Hudspeth County in western Texas...

* WHEN...Until 200 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos. Some low-water
crossings may become impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 954 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause arroyo and small stream flooding.
Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall of up to 0.5 to 1.5 inches is expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Dell City and Cornudas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles. Be especially cautious at night when it is
harder to recognize the dangers of flooding.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.
